title: It's really starting to look like a new StarCraft game will be revealed at BlizzCon
summary: Initial reports of a Nexon-developed shooter were met with doubt, but now something funky is happening with the StarCraft 2 website. And have you seen the BlizzCon schedule?
body: I don't want to get anybody's hopes up, but with BlizzCon 2026 now just over a week away, it really is starting to look like something—possibly something big —is happening in the world of StarCraft. The excitement began earlier this week when Korea's Chosun ( Google translated , via WCCFTech ) ran a story saying Nexon is close to finalizing a deal to develop a new game based on the StarCraft series. As Chosun noted, the series has been dormant since StarCraft Remastered in 2017; the last original StarCraft game, StarCraft 2, arrived all the way back in 2010. Despite that, the series remains hugely popular in Korea. The StarCraft subreddit took some issues with the report: For one thing, Chosun suggested the new game would be StarCraft 3, rather than the StarCraft shooter Nexon is reportedly working on . There are also concerns that the report might be accurate, given CEO Junghun Lee's enthusiasm for generative AI and microtransactions. Still, the timing seemed right: BlizzCon 2026 runs September 12-13, which is now less than two weeks away. title: Microsoft announces cap on Xbox Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers, admits most aren't using it much anyway
summary: Gotta find revenue wherever you can, I guess.
body: As Microsoft continues to flail for a remedy to the reputational damage it's incurred as a result of its repeated mass layoffs , bungled industry consolidation strategies , and partnership with Israeli surveillance agencies , its gaming division is returning to a favorite page from its playbook in recent years: Hiking service costs. Today, Xbox announced that it will implement a monthly cap on Xbox Cloud Gaming hours for Game Pass subscribers. Previously, eligible Game Pass users could use the game streaming service without a time limit; Beginning in November, however, they'll need to purchase additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store once they expend their allotted cloud gaming hours. The Cloud Gaming hourly limits will be determined by Game Pass subscription tier: Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Xbox acknowledged that the rollout of a monthly time limit on cloud gaming hours is "a meaningful change, particularly for players who regularly spend more time gaming through the cloud." title: DLSS 5 can be jammed into almost any game now, so I've been playing FM26 with neural rendered little computer people because that's just what I do
summary: And here's how I did it.
body: Ever since the Control mod appeared I've been enjoying jamming the released DLSS 5 .dll files into a bunch of different games, to greater or lesser effect. Some games it works well in, some it doesn't quite take and you end up with visuals that look a lot like the characters have worms writhing around under their skin. Though, I have to say when I stuck it into the review version of The Blood of Dawnwalker and it failed to hook the DLSS pipeline that look kinda worked for my semi-Vrakhiri. Bit of extra undead chic with the game failing to run the DLSS neural rendering feature with actual motion vectors or scene depth. With the necessary files being released in the early access version of NBA 2K27, they've now been unleashed across the internet and modders have been busy getting game-agnostic versions ready for people to squeeze into any title they fancy. And while the first iteration was focused on Control and then games running DLSS already, there have been mods released—particularly the RenoDX and specifically the ShortFuse mods—which allow you to experiment with pushing DLSS 5 into practically any game you like. title: A multi-month delay for Deus Ex turned into a huge payoff for one of its best characters, says designer Harvey Smith
summary: Smith's story about the late stages of Deus Ex development takes some time to get to the point, but it's a fun ride.
body: Nobody likes game delays. Sure, a delay is temporary and suck is forever , as Gabe Newell once said, but it still chafes. But sometimes a little extra development time can go a very long way. In a new interview with the NoClip podcast , immersive sim maestro Harvey Smith shared one such story about Deus Ex, explaining how it leveraged some extra post-production time to give a much bigger role to one of the game's most famous NPCs—and make it a much better game in the process. Smith's tale actually followed a remark by Ben Horne, his co-founder at the new Black Pony Immersive studio, who said, "You can elevate a good immersive sim into a great immersive sim in a very short amount of time, a matter of months, if you just protect a post-production time." Publishers generally don't want to hear that, Smith added—although he obviously agrees with the sentiment—and so 20-some years ago, when Ion Storm Austin asked Eidos for more time to tighten up Deus Ex, "We geared up for this giant fight." Instead, Eidos just said yes. "They were so distracted by what was happening in Dallas with Daikatana and such that they were like, 'Sure, sure, sure. Take five more months, take six more, whatever…

title: The bizarre spirit of classic Elder Scrolls games is alive and well in little lo-fi RPG A Short Quest
summary: A few hours with a recent playtest has me eager to play the full thing next year.
body: When a big old tree talks, I listen. He said, "I have a task of great importance," as soon as I opened my eyes, and who was I to turn him down? "Take this note to the King, it should be a short quest," he instructed, and although there is no king in the playtest for A Short Quest , I am eager to fulfill the tree's wishes when the whole game is out next year. There are actually a lot of mysterious things I found in the few hours I spent with A Short Quest that I'd like to know more about. Every time I passed by a pond it spoke and asked me to dance (jump three times) for a blueberry. I found a note in an old mine that told me how to find the "glyph cipher" on the side of a cart, but I still don't know what to do with it. And I'm still not sure why I was summoned into the underground domain of a ghost wizard who tried to kill me. A Short Quest reminded me of when I would watch a friend from middle school play Morrowind on his Xbox or when I played Oblivion for the first time. It's a lo-fi first-person RPG that's trying to evoke that earlier, goofier era of the form; back when an elf would fall out of the sky and drop a scroll of flight as a joke. The little pocket of A Short Quest's…

title: Guild Wars 3 is a lot smaller scale than Guild Wars 2 because of the new approach to combat and movement: 'You would probably see about 20 players in a large combat scenario'
summary: Expect more clarity, but no more 100-player boss fights.
body: At Gamescom, I got to see a hands-off demo of Guild Wars 3 and chatted to the developers about what they have in store for us when the MMO hits beta next year. You can read about the significant changes to movement and combat in my Guild Wars 3 preview , but we also discussed how different the upcoming MMO's scale will be when compared to its predecessors. Guild Wars 3 sits between OG Guild Wars, which was very small scale, and Guild Wars 2, where you could fight a boss with a hundred other players. It still has that multiplayer focus, but compared to Guild Wars 2, ArenaNet has significantly reduced how many people you'll be playing with at once. "At most, out in the open world, you would probably see about 20 players in a large combat scenario," says game director Colin Johanson. "Our movement systems and our combat systems, in particular, are really high fidelity. They're designed to lend themselves to being able to see everything that's going on, and we felt like that number is where it starts to cap out. You start losing some of the visceral sense of what the gameplay is like." Johnason adds that, at the high end of player numbers, the action starts to become "more spectacle t…

title: Zach Cregger doesn't want to get bogged down in 'the wild aspects' of Resident Evil's lore: 'I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat'
summary: The trench coat is actually integral to the build.
body: What's the weirdest bit of Resident Evil lore you know of? Is it the fact that Claire Redfield's favourite food is a cheeseburger? Maybe it's that Hunk spent a week lost in Raccoon City's sewers eating rats after getting his ass beaten by Birkin? Or perhaps it's that the Tyrant's trench coat is more than just a bold fashion statement—it's actually integral to the build. There's been a few explanations as to why Tyrants wear trench coats in Resident Evil games. One perk of the coat is that it helps disguise the mutations, which allows Tyrants to infiltrate more sensitive areas, but its biggest bonus is its power-limiting function. Wearing the trench coat holds the Tyrant together by preventing out-of-control mutations, and if it's damaged or the Tyrant removes it you'll get a Super Tyrant. (Image credit: Capcom) You'd be forgiven for not knowing this as it's not exactly a widely talked about tidbit, which is exactly why Zach Cregger, director of the upcoming Resident Evil movie, is staying away from Resident Evil's deep lore: to keep the film as grounded as possible. title: Both Microsoft and Sony say they're under no obligation to pass tariff refunds on to customers
summary: One for me, none for thee.
body: Tech tariffs imposed by the Trump administration were ruled unconstitutional back in February , though the saga is far from over. Many companies have since sought refunds, and consumers battling rising hardware prices are wondering whether they'll see those recouped costs trickle down. Well, as far as major players Microsoft and Sony are concerned, the answer is 'No.' To rewind a smidge, consoles have been climbing in price for some time now. An Xbox gamer filed a proposed class-action lawsuit against Microsoft back in July , accusing the company of passing on the cost of tariffs to consumers. A similar lawsuit was filed against Sony back in May . Now, lawyers from both companies are arguing that their respective sides are simply under no obligation to pass on tariff refunds to customers. As reported by Game File , Microsoft’s legal team filed a motion to dismiss its lawsuit last month, saying, "There is nothing unjust about Plaintiff purchasing an Xbox at an advertised price and getting exactly what he paid for—regardless of whatever theory he devised months later about Microsoft’s cost structure." It looks like you can go pretty ham on some Sims-style building within those stony walls, too—the trailer shows a tool which you can drag to build walls and rooms inside the castle. Yup, just like The Sims! There's a whole bunch of furniture as well, including a slightly unusual framed portrait of a tiger that Kliff has deigned to display outside his home, for whatever reason. It looks like you'll be able to build a village around this castle as well, perhaps similar to the Greymanes camp you form in the main game. There are people cooking, little village stalls, and plenty of chatter that seems to be happening either within the castle walls or just outside of them. title: PUBG's new spin-off game is 'faster, meaner, and more aggressive' with sword hands and 'a little bit of light cannibalism'
summary: "PUBG is deliberate and thoughtful and tactical. This is not that."
body: PUBG remains one of Steam's most-played games, which makes it all the more surprising that PUBG Studios and publisher Krafton haven't made more attempts to milk it over the years. PUBG: DED NET might be the biggest yank of the udder to date though, revealing an entirely new spin-off roguelite FPS set in the '90s. And if you didn't know the game was set in the '90s, you sure will after the game's trailer beats you over the head with period-accurate vibes. Creative director Dave Curd helpfully informs me that the "DED" in DED NET stands for "dog eat dog," which makes the words emblazoned across one of the miniguns in the trailer make a whole lot more sense. I've sat down with Curd in the hours after the game's reveal at Gamescom's Opening Night Live, where he tells me a little bit more about what players can expect from DED NET. Curd says DED NET is going to be "unhinged" and "unfiltered" with the promise of tons of build variety that'll unfurl the more matches you play. "Every run starts different, and you'll always have something in mind. Maybe this run I want to be the very close quartered, door kicker, riot shield guy. title: Guild Wars 3's approach to combat and movement is like nothing I've ever seen in an MMO before: 'One of our big goals when we make a new game in the Guild Wars franchise is to set out and try new things'
summary: Wall running, mantling, aerial attacks, multiplayer combos—it's a lot of new stuff.
body: There are few things as exciting as the prospect of a new MMO. And when that new MMO is from ArenaNet, the studio that's been focused on Guild Wars for more than two decades, the excitement is even greater. Having seen Guild Wars 3 in action at Gamescom, and spoken to game director Colin Johanson and lead combat designer Kevin Stocker, my excitement has been justified. Just as Guild Wars 2 was dramatically different from its predecessor, Guild Wars 3 is not a simple sequel. It's distinct from GW2, a very different kind of MMO, and one that even in the short space of time I spent watching it being played is full of novel ideas. (Image credit: ArenaNet) The first big change is in its setting. The clock has been turned back 1,000 years, and we're heading to Orr—a land that in GW2's era is a post-apocalyptic hellscape, but at this earlier point is a verdant wilderness teeming with spirits. "The origins of the Guild Wars franchise originate out of Orr," says Johanson. "This is a time before the gods have left the world, very shortly after Grenth has usurped Dhuum and become the god of death. This is a time where the first guilds are starting to rise across the world, and before the ver…

title: Acer's bizarre hybrid handheld/laptop concept is way more interesting than what is actually getting released this year
summary: Flippin' 'eck.
body: While I've bemoaned the expensive state of handheld gaming PCs at length , that doesn't mean I find a cool concept model any less head-turning. Enter Acer's latest Project DualPlay creation: a handheld gaming PC with a flippable screen that can turn into a laptop. The Project DualPlay Mini was shown off on-stage at IFA 2026, in Berlin . It's all about reimagining "what a gaming handheld form factor can do," exploring a design that functions "both as a gaming handheld and as a mobile productivity station," according to Acer . As a concept machine, however, the Project DualPlay Mini might not see the light of day beyond the IFA stage. What will see a wide release later this year, though, is the Acer Predator Atlas 7. Very simply, this is a cut-down version of Acer's chunkier Predator Atlas 8 handheld . For starters, the seven-inch touchscreen still enjoys a 120 Hz refresh rate and 500 nits of peak brightness. The device also has an 80Whr battery, and the guts of this new seven-inch form factor still includes Intel Arc B390 graphics, and an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor. title: Gigabyte GO27Q24A Review
summary: An affordable QD-OLED gaming monitor that’s got it where it counts.
body: We’ve been reviewing some silly-priced gaming monitors in recent times but, some of the latest-and-greatest models wield premium features that are unnecessary for many buyers. Gigabyte’s GO27Q24A strives to keep things simple by stripping-away some of the less-universally popular, expensive technologies to produce a spartan gaming monitor that focuses on the category’s most-important facets, to keep the price down. Gigabyte has successfully done this before using WOLED and Tandem OLED panels in the same range, so how will this QD-OLED model fare? Assembling the Gigabyte GO27Q24A is simple: the stem clips to the screen and the stand uses a single thumbscrew to attach to the stem without any tools being needed. The stand is the same, solid, small-footprint unit that Gigabyte’s premium monitors use and it lets competitive types sit right up close to the screen. The stem is also the same seen on its superior siblings and affords a generous degree of manipulation to get the screen sitting just so: there’s -5°~+21° tilt, ±15° swivel and 90° pivot. Asked about Sirius, Gnaś mentioned the recent cuts to the development team , saying—as CD Projekt did when the layoffs happened—that the changes were made to meet "the current needs of the project." title: How to sell silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: The Vrakhiri's reign makes it hard to find a merchant buying silver.
body: I had no trouble finding vendors to offload Coen's endless supply of low-value pilfered junk in Blood of Dawnwalker , but it took a few days to figure out how to sell silver . It makes sense that silver is considered contraband under vampire rule, so you have to find the right vendor to foist it on and complete a quick quest before adventuring south. Where can you sell silver in Blood of Dawnwalker? (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) You can sell silver in Svartrau City to the aptly named Silver Trader, but before you leave Coen's home in Laslea Glen, complete the Into the Den quest. It doesn't take long to slay the ravenous bear, and you need the intel uncovered by investigating what remains of its dinner. Any item with a white chalice icon is silver contraband Complete Into the Den, a quest that begins east of the Northern Foothill Head south to Svatrau City and speak with the Silver Trader Tell him you know he's dealing in silver, and he'll agree to trade In the name of RPG science, I tried heading to Svartrau immediately and skipping Into the Den, but the Silver Trader just tells Coen to get lost. You've gotta kill the bear, sorry. A note at the end of the quest points Coen to Svart…

title: How to save Vlad in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Can you control yourself?
body: If you're curious whether you can save Vlad in Blood of Dawnwalker , chances are you've probably just killed him. Unable to resist your newly-gained vampiric urges, you chomped his neck and drank his blood, and the game didn't give you a choice in the matter. Well, there is a way Vlad can survive your encounter after he leaves the burning house, towards the end of the prologue. Obviously, this will contain spoilers for this final section of the prologue , so leave 10 seconds ago if you're here by accident. How to save Vlad in Blood of Dawnwalker Make sure to beat the miniboss with at least one health segment left Rebel Wolves This will allow you to control the hunger when you speak to Vlad Rebel Wolves If you want Vlad to survive the conversation you two have when he exits the burning house, you need to have more than one health segment . Since health is blood for vampires, when you're one segment or below, you're hungry, which impacts your conversations with human characters, i.e. makes you want to eat them. If you are below one segment when you convince Vlad to leave the burning house, you're unable to resist your hunger and you kill him. If you're above one segment, though, you…

title: Should you spare Xanthe in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
summary: Make a deal with this ancient Vrakhiri or send her packing.
body: Deciding whether to spare Xanthe and make a deal in Blood of Dawnwalker is a really tough choice. On the one hand, she's an evil ancient vampire who kidnapped and killed a bunch of innocent women, but she was only using Brencis as a tool of convenience. That might be enough for you to ponder what advantage an alliance with her could bring. Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers for Xanthe's The Cycle of Love quest , but otherwise, here's the outcome if you spare her. Should you spare Xanthe in Blood of Dawnwalker? Killing Xanthe will make your castle assault a bit harder Rebel Wolves If you kill Xanthe you'll also have to decide Chariklea's fate Rebel Wolves The main impact of sparing Xanthe in her mansion, when you defeat her during The Cycle of Love quest, is that during the final assault on Griefberg Castle: You won't have to fight any Blood Guard enemies. Xanthe will meet you in the castle and offer some advice. You won't have to go through the nightmare sequence you get if you kill Xanthe. Is this worth it for letting the Vrakhiri live? Not really. If you kill Xanthe, you won't have to fight her in the castle either, so the only real advantage allying with her gives you …

title: How to beat the Ravenous Bear and complete Into the Den in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Kill this hangry boss and find the flat stone marked with X.
body: Fighting the Ravenous Bear is an early combat challenge in Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, but mainly because you don't have many skills or decent equipment yet, which turns the fight into a slog. After you do defeat it, you'll also have to track down a treasure as part of the Into the Den quest. I'll run through how to do both below. How to beat the Ravenous Bear in Blood of Dawnwalker The Ravenous Bear is the most challenging early boss you can encounter near Laslea. Here are some tips to beat it, plus a video of me fighting the bear above so you can see the strategy in action: Get a better sword : The fight will be over faster if you get a decent weapon. I recommend heading across to the other side of the lake, looking for the big tree with the wolves, and completing the Deep Down quest. This will get you the Undead Warrior's Sword, which is a nice upgrade over what you had. Parry its regular attacks, but dodge to the side of its red unblockable ones : Parrying is better in this fight because you're less likely to run out stamina (which dodging consumes), so you can keep attacking. When the bear attacks with a red skull, dodge to the side, rather than away. This will give you …

title: I've spent over 80 hours in The Blood of Dawnwalker—here are my top 20 quick tips to survive Vale Sangora
summary: Help Coen rescue his family from Vrakhiri clutches.
body: Searching for some Blood of Dawnwalker tips ? Deciding what to do first in this vampiric RPG can be tough, especially if you're the kind of person who's paralysed by indecision when a game gives you a lot of freedom. You've got 30 days to save your family: everything else is pretty much anyone's game. (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) There's no right or wrong answer. You can't really fail The Blood of Dawnwalker either, depending on how you define failure. While its time constraints form a guideline and structure to follow, where to spend that time is entirely down to you. Here's my best advice from spending 80 hours with the game, testing its many quests and choices. 1. Use the shield icon to Perfect Block Rather than timing your block to the enemy's swing, wait for when the shield turns orange on the directional indicator. Also unlock Perfect Riposte for a guaranteed crit afterwards. 2. Take time to level up I barely levelled in my run because I was worried about time and I made it to the end of the story with a whole 15 days left. Don't be like me. 3. Killing enemies is time-efficient Murdering enemies you find, particularly wolves, boar, and bear bosses in the woods, is an extreme…

title: How to prepare Anca's recipe in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Fix your mother's medicine with the right steps.
body: During Blood of Dawnwalker 's main prologue quest, Withering Away, you'll have to prepare Anca's recipe into a medicine for your mother's anxiety, helping her overcome her fear to attend the Blood Mass that evening. Anca gives you a page of instructions to follow, but the tricksy game won't let you view them while making the medicine. This means you're up a creek if you haven't already memorised them, and don't want to potentially load a save in the distant past just to read a sheet of paper. I'll include the instructions below, along with the friendly advice that it is very important that you make this medicine correctly. How to prepare Anca's recipe in Blood of Dawnwalker Use hot water Rebel Wolves Add three spoonfuls of herbs Rebel Wolves Once you arrive back at the house, your father will ask you to prepare the medicine for your mother. Unfortunately, you can't read the recipe at this point, so you have to have it memorised, or just follow the instructions below: Choose the 'Use hot water' option Choose the 'Add three spoonfuls of herbs' option This follows Anca's instructions that she gave you, and will help make the correct medicine for Esme so she can have a slightly more r…

title: Can you beat Brencis in The Blood of Dawnwalker's prologue?
summary: Face the big bad a little earlier than expected.
body: At the end of Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, you'll fight Brencis , the Knyaz of Vale Sangora, and quite obviously the game's main antagonist. It's one of those classic "you're not supposed to win this" boss fights, since losing to him plays a cutscene and continues the story. But where there's a will, there's a way. Below I'll explain what happens if you beat Brencis, provide a video of fighting him, and the outcome. Be warned, this contains spoilers for some aspects of the game's ending sequence. Can you beat Brencis in Blood of Dawnwalker's prologue? The answer to this is a little complex—both yes and probably no. You can beat Brencis in your first fight with him provided you've learnt how to Perfect Block and dodge, though it will take a little while. After you beat Brencis, a cutscene will play in which he effectively pulls you into hell and reveals his true form, Brencis, Grotesque Ascendant (also the final boss). Since this is still a boss fight, you theoretically should be able to beat it, but even after acquiring the strongest equipment I could on the first day, you do an incredibly small amount of damage to him, and one hit from him will invariably kill you, even if yo…

title: Every romancable character in The Blood of Dawnwalker and how to have them fall fang over heels for Coen
summary: Coen has three options for a bat romance.
body: Coen is certainly going through it, but Blood of Dawnwalker offers a smidge of succor by not making him face the onslaught of horrors alone. You've got three potential romance options for him—one of which seems more 'canonical' than the rest—and the vampy RPG doesn't make you choose just one. When it comes to games like this, I love to kiss and tell. So here are all three of your options for love in a breezy Blood of Dawnwalker romance guide . Spoiler warning: While we keep details as minimal as possible, this guide follows all three romance plots through the end of the game. That includes details on how to ensure your lover shows up in the epilogue, so keep that in mind before you go skimming through the text. How romance works in The Blood of Dawnwalker The Blood of Dawnwalker has three romanceable characters: Anca, Lacra, and Crake. Coen isn't limited to just one partner either, so don't fret over fumbling your shot. RPG veterans won't find much out of the ordinary when it comes to wooing your fantasy lover, but here's the gist of how romance works in Blood of Dawnwalker: The most important step is knowing where to start each romance and prioritizing chances to flirt with your …

title: How to drink Vrakhir blood in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Chow down to unlock new vampiric abilities.
body: Finding Vrakhir blood in Blood of Dawnwalker might trip you up a bit if you're looking to unlock new abilities and generally mess about as a creature of the night. While you acquire most skills in the tree naturally as you drink blood and just generally be a vampire, some specific skills only become available when you "drink Vrakhir blood" and it's not clear exactly how. Below, I'll explain where to get it, plus how to unlock all Vrakhir blood-related abilities. How to drink Vrakhir blood in Blood of Dawnwalker If you anger one of the Vrakhiri boyars by messing with their operation, you'll get a chance to fight them (and drink their blood) Rebel Wolves You can also get Vrakhir blood by defeating certain Murohn bosses, such as the one in the Bad Blood quest in St. Tyna's Grove Rebel Wolves You can also get Vrakhir blood from some of Xanthe's quests Rebel Wolves The main way you drink Vrakhir blood is by defeating the game's Vrakhir bosses , namely, Ambrus, Bakir, and Xanthe, and then choosing to drink from them. Supping the blood of these three vampires unlocks different abilities, namely: Ambrus - Scarlet Shield Bakir - Shadowstorm Xanthe - Blood Surge Unlike earning skills by con…

title: Should you let Anca use The Font in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
summary: Cleanse the herbalist's curse or use it yourself.
body: Choosing whether to let Anca use The Font or claim it for yourself in Blood of Dawnwalker is tough. On the one hand, you committed a lot of time to fighting your way through an ancient ruin and it'd be nice to have something to show for it. On the other hand, you've got Anca's fate to consider. This guide will contain spoilers for Anca's questline , plus the effect of this choice. All that said, here's the impact of each option. Should you let Anca use The Font in Blood of Dawnwalker? (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) When you arrive in the chamber of The Font in Anca's Stronger Than Achilles quest, you'll find there's only enough tasty blood left for either you or Anca. You'll be given three choices: "If it's alright with you - I'll use it." "Go ahead. Make what you will with it." "We should destroy it." I'll run through each decision and outcome below. 1. Coen uses The Font If Coen uses it he gains the Font of Life health regeneration perk when human (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) If you use the blood yourself, you'll gain the Font of Life passive, which regenerates human health during the day. This is a pretty decent perk, especially when Witchcraft abilities cost HP, but it's worth n…

title: How to complete The Heart Wants What It Wants in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Help Ocha and Nora find a new life.
body: When you stumble on The Heart Wants What It Wants in a random tavern in Blood of Dawnwalker , you might be surprised by how complex this quest can be in terms of its outcomes. The actual meat of the quest, helping an Uriashi, Ocha, and her friend, Nora, escape the clutches of Svartrau's crime lord, is pretty simple, but it can end in many different ways. Here's how to complete the quest, plus its different outcomes based on your choices. How to complete The Heart Wants What It Wants in Blood of Dawnwalker Use vampiric powers to get onto the balcony at night and steal Andrei's ring from his desk Rebel Wolves The ring is the correct memento for Ocha's spell Rebel Wolves Open the pig pen to distract the guard then draw the hex on the window Rebel Wolves If you go downstairs or give Ocha the wrong item, you'll have to kill Andrei, which impacts the overall outcome Rebel Wolves Once you acquire the quest from Ocha and Nora at the Altenmarkt inn, follow the map marker to Andrei's butcher shop, and enter via the balcony on the upper floor using your vampire powers. In the upper room you'll find three different mementos for Ocha's amnesia spell: a ring, a pendant, and a cleaver. The memen…

title: How to complete Forge It Anew in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Track down the sword shard locations and the right blacksmith.
body: The Forge It Anew quest in Blood of Dawnwalker sees you trying to reforge St. Mihai's Silver Sword after you acquired it during A Monk and a Saint. Vrakhiri aren't very fond of silver, as you've likely surmised, so this sword will make for a potent vampire-slaying tool. You'll have to track down the missing sword shards and then a blacksmith to put them all together, so here's where to look. How to complete Forge It Anew in Blood of Dawnwalker Read the note in St. Mihai's coffin after you defeat him to start the quest (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) There are three sword shards located in Kobold nests around Vale Sangora that you need to find before you can reforge the Sword of St. Mihai. First sword shard location The first shard is in a Kobold nest in the northeast of the Maragir Wealds Rebel Wolves Defeat the Kobolds then grab the shard from the broken cross Rebel Wolves The first sword shard is located in the northeast corner of the Maragir Wealds , to the northeast of the Upper Maragir Wealds shrine, across the river. You'll find a cave, along with a trail you can follow, which begins the Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb quest. Pursue the trail into the Kobold den, kill them, and t…

title: How to complete Home Sweet Home in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Escape Aurelius's endless dream.
body: Finding a way to escape the neverending nightmare of Home Sweet Home in Blood of Dawnwalker took me longer than I'd care to admit. Like me, you probably thought defeating Aurelius in The Silts Tower would be a quick in-out jobbie, but now you're trapped in a grindy dream sequence defeating endless tides of spectres. Fear not, though, there is a way to escape the dream, and I'll explain how below. If you're here and haven't encountered this quest yet, firstly, why? Secondly, leave now so as not to spoil yourself. How to complete Home Sweet Home in Blood of Dawnwalker You need to investigate the well in the village area where you rescue your siblings from ghosts Rebel Wolves You'll speak to your reflection and open up a new route to take through the dream Rebel Wolves In the church, interact with the yellow-marked figures based on what the priest is saying Rebel Wolves After you run through the dream sequence once, having breakfast with your family, watching as they're kidnapped by a flying monster, then saving them all and heading to the church, you'll realise you're stuck in a time loop. In fact, I completed this whole sequence twice, after which, even the same dialogue repeats. T…

title: How to complete Letters to Lunka in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Help the Sanzhani to send secret messages to Lunka.
body: The Letters to Lunka quest in Blood of Dawnwalker is a sneaky way to get a bit more intel about what's happening with Coen's family in Griefberg Castle. As you likely discovered in the Good Home quest, these fairies can spirit themselves into the dungeon and whisper messages in Lunka's ear. If you help out the Sanzhani around the map, you can ask all remaining questions—here's how it works. How to complete Letters to Lunka in Blood of Dawnwalker You can send one message to Lunka for each Sanzhani you help (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) After you finish the Good Home quest and accept your reward of sending your first letter to Lunka, you can send four more letters, one per Sanzhani quest you complete around Vale Sangora. Whenever you send a new letter, a new quest will appear for you to complete, so don't forget to send one back at the main burrow each time. The order these quests appear on the map is linked to which letters you send , but either way, it'll be one of the following locations marked by a ? below: Burrow Sorrows The Burrow Sorrows quest is in the forest in the northwest of The Rockfalls region (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) This quest marker shows up in the northwest of t…

title: Should you invite Ambrus in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
summary: Send this Vrakhir to hell or keep him around.
body: Deciding whether to invite Ambrus in is a tough choice in Blood of Dawnwalker , especially as you don't really know what "invite" means in this context. This rogue-ish Vrakhir certainly deserves hell for all the atrocities he committed bleeding Vale Sangora's subjects, but maybe there's more to him than meets the eye. Obviously, this guide will contain spoilers as to the immediate and eventual impact of this choice, so leave now if you don't want to know. Should you invite Ambrus in Blood of Dawnwalker? You'll have to decide whether to invite Ambrus if you drink his blood (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) If you invite Ambrus in, the main consequence is that he'll talk to you throughout the rest of the game . I'm not talking full blown dialogue, but he'll essentially make comments as a voice inside your head, about stuff you're doing, such as when you make a choice, or in combat. In fact, there's one Ambrus comment at a particular moment (I won't spoil it) that made me laugh so much I consider it well worth inviting him just for that. Does it have any consequences? Basically, no. The main impact is that Ambrus will help you a bit in the final boss, but he can also be turned against you…

title: Should you force feed Esme in The Blood of Dawnwalker?
summary: Get some scran in Coen's mum.
body: Deciding whether to force feed Coen's mum in Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the initial choices you'll encounter, but if you're like me, you may pause over it a while wondering how much it's going to impact. The game's prologue has only just started in earnest, and this is the first proper decision you encounter after all. So, here's what happens based on either choice and which I recommend picking. Should you force feed Coen's mum in Blood of Dawnwalker? Trying to force feed Esme is indeed bad (Image credit: Rebel Wolves) While Esme indeed does need to eat—how else is she going to make lots of lovely blood for mass in the evening—force feeding her doesn't help the situation. If you choose the "Alright. Let's try" option, Coen will pick up the spoon and try to force feed Esme, but this results in her smacking the spoon aside and then essentially bursting into tears, leaving your dad, Pieter, feeling very sorry about what he tried to do. Choosing the "I won't feed her against her will" option instead sees your father try to force feed her, but she also still bats the spoon out of his hand. It's the same result, but this way she at least seems less distressed with the outcome. This d…

title: How to complete Where Loyalty Lies in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Join the Manumits by increasing your infamy.
body: Completing Where Loyalty Lies is the first big step in aligning yourself with a faction in Blood of Dawnwalker . Until now, you've likely been taking the fight to Brencis yourself, though maybe you decided to free Mert out of the goodness of your heart. But to join the Manumits, you'll have to prove your commitment to the cause by raising your infamy, a system you may not have interacted with much until now. How to complete Where Loyalty Lies in Blood of Dawnwalker Angering and defeating a Vrakhiri boyar (like Ambrus) is a great way to earn infamy Rebel Wolves Crushing Soldier Camps is a very time-effective way of getting infamy since they only cost one cycle Rebel Wolves The same goes for the Soldier Pickets that start appearing when you reach infamy Level 2 Rebel Wolves You'll need to raise your infamy level to Notorious in order to join the Manumits, which is the fourth (IV) level on the court's infamy track, which you can see in the 'Court' tab of the menu. Your best bet for raising infamy is: Complete named Vrakhir quests in any of the regions , such as Ambrus's Cellars, Ambrus's Transports, Ambrus's Collectors, or Ambrus's Prisoners, all of which are available in the regions…

title: How to complete Blasphemy in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Help Gremla track down the stolen tapestry before nightfall.
body: The Blasphemy quest is one of the most impactful in Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, since it impacts the Blood Mass at the end of the day. When you find Gremla, bemoaning the theft of her tapestry, she explains that she took on that task of weaving a vampiric banner for the Knyaz, and that Brencis won't be pleased if she can't get it back. It's easy enough to see the writing on the wall as to the outcome for not completing this one. However, the quest's second section, which sees you searching for the culprit, is actually quite tough. Below, I'll run through the whole quest, plus I've included details as to the outcome and rewards for getting Gremla's tapestry back, or keeping the thief's secret. How to complete Blasphemy in Blood of Dawnwalker Investigate the loom in Gremla's house Rebel Wolves Investigate the footprints and walking stick trail leading to the torn scrap Rebel Wolves Examine the torn scrap and find the blood stain Rebel Wolves After you speak to Gremla at her house in Laslea, you need to use Focus Mode (right click) to do some investigating: Use Focus Mode to inspect the weaving loom in her house Inspect the trail of footprints and the cane trail around the side …

title: How to free Mert in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Complete Under Watchful Eyes without battling through the entire fort.
body: Finding a way to free Mert in Blood of Dawnwalker 's Under Watchful Eyes quest took me a while to work out. At first, I slaughtered the entire fort, but after such a slog of a fight I realised there must be a better way to do it—turns out there is. You can take a sneakier route at nighttime which drastically reduces the number of soldiers you have to kill. In my video runthrough of it below, I also show how to reduce the number of fights even further with some tactically-employed Voracious Bites. Here's how to free Mert without murdering the fort. How to free Mert without killing everyone in Stoneward Post There's an obvious approach to freeing Mert in Under Watchful Eyes, and that's killing every soldier in the fort, but this is understandably quite tricky. There is a sneakier route you can take via a back door instead which will really cut down the number of goons you've got to put down. You can avoid the two-on-one fight in Friedo's office by following my exact route in the video above. To do it, you need to purchase the Shadow Dweller and Dimension Reach upgrades in the Vampirism tree so you can take a shortcut up to the battlements. These are generally very handy upgrades, th…

title: All Swordmastery ability manual locations in The Blood of Dawnwalker
summary: Unlock these blade skills early.
body: Tracking down Swordmastery manuals in Blood of Dawnwalker will give you more abilities to use when fighting in your human form. While the regular skill manuals appear to be random, the actual ability manuals have fixed locations, so you can track them down whenever you want. Below, I've included manual locations for all the Swordmastery abilities in the optimal order for grabbing them. All Swordmastery ability locations There are seven Swordmastery abilities in Blood of Dawnwalker. You start with Dirty Trick already unlocked, but you can get the others through certain quests or by finding manuals, usually in Bandit Camps, Soldier Camps, or purchase via Swordmastery trainers. The trainers I know of are: Merchant Location Ursul Complete the Ambrus Prisoners: Lucky Crossing quest north of Svartrau and then head to Ursul's camp.
